messages:
sophie: FYI we just got an escalation from Acme — multiple accounts reporting streaming responses cut mid-token and clients seeing a \"broken pipe\". They say it started after a recent model swap. Ticket attached: https://acme.support/tkt/4321

sophie: errors in their logs look like `recv: Connection reset by peer` and our gateway shows 502s spiking in the streaming route (\/v1/streams). They insist they didn't cancel, so we need to repro + confirm classification.

devon: assigning to oncall to triage — @nora can you take a look? I'm seeing the same 502 surge on the dashboard starting 2024-06-28 17:10 UTC.

nora: I'll take it. quick glance at logs: several entries like: `proxy: upstream read error: unexpected EOF while reading chunked body` and distinct `client aborted` traces. But sample traces also show `write failed: broken pipe` from our node.

nora: hypothesis: client-side TCP reset (RST) or `ECONNRESET` is being surfaced by the gateway as a 5xx. If we treat that as a client abort (499), we shouldn't count it as a server error. Need to confirm where the classification happens in the pipeline.

sophie: Repro steps the customer sent (they could reproduce reliably):
```
# stream request
curl -N -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" \
  -d $'{"prompt":"long stream test"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams
# then ctrl-c the client after ~2s
```
They say they didn't ctrl-c; but we can use this to reproduce the effect locally.

devon: I tried running `curl -N` and severing the connection with `kill -9` on the curl process — server logs show `write to client failed: broken pipe` and the metric pipeline currently increments `5xx_count` for `gateway_write_error`.

nora: here's a snippet from our gateway log (sanitized):
```
2024-06-28T17:12:03.123Z gateway-02 stream=abc upstream_id=mdl-7 write_error="broken pipe" downstream_ip=10.20.30.45
2024-06-28T17:12:03.124Z proxy-ctrl  upstream_status=200 proxy_err="client reset" conn_err=ECONNRESET
```
We need to check: when `conn_err=ECONNRESET`, are we mapping to a 502/504 label or to a client-abort (499) metric? Right now metrics team says it's counted as 5xx.

sophie: Customer impact: occasional 502 in SDKs, we bill them for tokens but their client didn't get the rest of the stream. They're worried about retriable semantics.

nora: action plan: 1) add additional logging to the gateway to emit `error_class=client_abort` for ECONNRESET/EPIPE on the downstream socket; 2) update metrics mapping to not increment `5xx_count` for those classes; 3) add an eval that runs `curl` repro and verifies that downstream abort shows up as 499-like event instead of 5xx.

devon: sounds good. Also, we should audit where the `upstream_status` is synthesized. If we synthesize 502 on proxy write errors, we might be double-counting — cause is downstream abort, not upstream model failure.

nora: working on a patch. snippet of change I'm trying locally (pseudo):
```
if err in [EPIPE, ECONNRESET]:
  emit_metric('client_abort')
  mark_response(499)
else:
  emit_metric('gateway_5xx')
  mark_response(502)
```
Need to confirm any existing consumers that rely on the 5xx metric before flipping.

sophie: pinging metrics + support: @devon can you create a short-lived dashboard showing `gateway_5xx` vs `client_abort` so we can see historical baseline? Also flag CSMs so they can communicate to customers.

devon: on it — creating dashboard now. Also notified metrics@redwood for a quick hangout.

alerts-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-2331 — Streaming gateway write errors increase. Severity: P2. Owner: nora.

nora: deployed a candidate today to staging that changes the classification and adds the `conn_err` tag. Did a canary on gateway-02. I ran the `curl -N` + `kill -9` repro and verify: staging shows `client_abort` metric increment and no 5xx.

deploy-bot: deploy: routing update applied to gateway-02-candidate at 2024-06-28T19:05 UTC.

sophie: can we roll this change to prod but gated? I'd like low-risk rollout (canary + 20% traffic) and to keep historical aggregation unchanged until metrics team updates dashboards.

nora: will run a 20% canary for 30m then 50% for 30m. I'll also add a migration flag so the metric emitted is `client_abort.v2` so old dashboards won't break.

devon: dashboards show immediate improvement: `gateway_5xx` back down ~85% after the canary, `client_abort.v2` shows corresponding rise. Good sign.

sophie: communicated to customer that we're rolling a fix and asked them for any additional repro info (network middleboxes, proxies) — they replied they use a mobile SDK that has intermittent NAT timeouts; could explain resets.

nora: follow-ups: 1) open PR to route ECONNRESET/EPIPE to client-abort path (link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/gateway/pull/558); 2) metrics team to decide whether to backfill the data or keep separate `v2` metric; 3) add an e2e test in infra that simulates mid-stream TCP RST and asserts no server 5xx is recorded.

sophie: thanks @nora and @devon. I'll update the customer. Marking this thread resolved once we get a post-deploy confirmation. :white_check_mark:

nora: final status 2024-06-28T20:40 UTC — prod canary completed, 100% rollout done. Post-deploy checks: 5xx for streaming route dropped to baseline and customer confirmed reduced incidents. Closing.

devon: filing a short postmortem note in #postmortems with timelines + impact numbers.

sophie: closing thread. Good job all. :tada:
